react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of nine differentially abundant metabolites identified convergent perturbation of glutathione- and one-carbon metabolism in the treatment group. Reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all nine InChIKeys. RaMP multi-database ORA (merged Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) ranked "Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways" (WP:WP2525) fourth (FDR = 3.58e-04, fold-enrichment = 450.34) with glutathione (KEGG:C00051) and O-phospho-L-serine (phosphoserine, KEGG:C01005) as the two hitting metabolites. The same two metabolites appeared in "Amino acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells" (WP:WP5213, rank 1, FDR = 6.92e-05, fold-enrichment = 1422.13). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed glutathione metabolism (KEGG:hsa00480, p = 0.069) and the glycine/serine/threonine axis (KEGG:hsa00260, p = 0.080) with phosphoserine as the sole hitting compound. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis co-ranked "Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism" and "Xenobiotics metabolism" as its top hits (p = 0.005), both drawing on glutathione and phosphoserine. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR), and network m/z analysis (Mummichog) solidifies glutathione and phosphoserine as the driver metabolites anchoring a perturbed trans-sulfuration and one-carbon cycle. Coumarin (KEGG:C05851) appeared exclusively in the xenobiotics cluster, while pantothenic acid (KEGG:C00864) independently scored across RaMP and Mummichog in CoA/vitamin B5 biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00770, p = 0.049). The reactive xenobiotic benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (KEGG:C14853) and the Phase I/II modulators methimazole (KEGG:C07190) and beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928) implicate an oxidative stress and xenobiotic clearance response consistent with glutathione depletion and rerouting of one-carbon units through the trans-sulfuration pathway.
